topics.title: Did Toba's Eruption Nearly End Us 74,000 Years Ago?
topics.core_question: How big was the Toba eruption roughly 74,000 years ago, and did it really push early humans to the edge of extinction?
topics.why_they_click: The largest eruption of the last two million years may — or may not — have nearly wiped out our species, and the evidence genuinely splits scientists.
topics.data_source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program eruption catalogue; peer-reviewed Toba ash and ice-core studies; NOAA NCEI paleoclimate data
topics.evidence: Sits on two rising searches at once — 'ice age explained' (+1472%) and 'supervolcano' (+37%) — with the disaster-with-a-twist shape the backlog already proved.

topics.title: Marie Tharp: The Map That Proved Continents Move
topics.core_question: How did a hand-drawn map of the Atlantic seafloor turn a mocked idea into the theory of plate tectonics?
topics.why_they_click: An idea dismissed as impossible for decades was confirmed by a rift valley drawn in pen by a woman kept off the research ship.
topics.data_source: USGS 'This Dynamic Earth'; Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory archives; peer-reviewed Heezen–Tharp seafloor mapping papers
topics.evidence: 'plate tectonics explained' is rising +205% over five years and no backlog episode covers how the theory was actually proven.

topics.title: Why Earth Plunged Back Into Cold 12,900 Years Ago
topics.core_question: What stopped the last ice age's warming and threw the planet back into a thousand-year freeze?
topics.why_they_click: The world was warming, then reversed — and the cause is still argued over: a collapsed ocean current, or an impact nobody can find.
topics.data_source: NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology; Greenland ice cores (NGRIP and GISP2); peer-reviewed Younger Dryas studies
topics.evidence: 'ice age explained' is rising +1472% over five years, the fastest-growing search in the channel's own subject area.

topics.title: The 1811 Quakes That Rang Bells in Boston
topics.core_question: What caused the New Madrid earthquakes of 1811–1812, and can a major quake strike the middle of a continent again?
topics.why_they_click: The Mississippi reportedly ran backwards — and the fault zone sits under several US states with no plate boundary anywhere near it.
topics.data_source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (New Madrid seismic zone); peer-reviewed New Madrid paleoseismic studies
topics.evidence: 'biggest earthquake in history' is rising +38%, and the backlog's Chile 1960 and Tohoku episodes show this audience returns for record quakes.

topics.title: Tunguska 1908: The Explosion That Left No Crater
topics.core_question: What flattened a vast stretch of Siberian forest in 1908, and why is there no crater under it?
topics.why_they_click: Something burst over Siberia with a force compared to a nuclear weapon, decades before nuclear weapons existed — and the ground shows nothing.
topics.data_source: NASA Planetary Science and Near-Earth Object records; peer-reviewed Tunguska airburst modelling studies
topics.evidence: The backlog's Chicxulub episode proves demand for impact detective stories; this is the same evidence-first shape with an unsolved centre.

topics.title: Nevado del Ruiz: The Eruption That Killed 23,000
topics.core_question: Why did a relatively small eruption in Colombia kill roughly 23,000 people in 1985 when scientists had already mapped the danger?
topics.why_they_click: A hazard map existed, warnings went out, and the town still went to bed — this is a story about the gap between knowing and surviving.
topics.data_source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program (fatalities and eruption record); USGS Volcano Hazards Program; peer-reviewed Nevado del Ruiz lahar studies
topics.evidence: The same 'famous disaster with a twist most people never heard' framing that carried the channel's Mount St. Helens episode.

topics.title: Campi Flegrei: The Supervolcano Lifting a Town
topics.core_question: Why does the ground under Pozzuoli rise and fall, and what does the Campi Flegrei record show this caldera has done before?
topics.why_they_click: Towns sit inside a caldera whose floor moves measurably year on year — and the old shoreline is now metres above your head.
topics.data_source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program; INGV (Italian National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology) monitoring data; NASA and ESA ground-deformation imagery
topics.evidence: 'supervolcano' is rising +37%, and this gives the channel a location-specific caldera story distinct from its Yellowstone myth-buster.

topics.title: The 1755 Lisbon Quake That Started a Science
topics.core_question: How did one morning of earthquake, tsunami and fire in 1755 become the beginning of modern seismology?
topics.why_they_click: Three catastrophes struck the same city in one morning, and the questionnaires sent afterwards are the first real earthquake survey in history.
topics.data_source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program; NOAA NCEI Global Historical Tsunami Database; peer-reviewed Lisbon 1755 studies
topics.evidence: 'biggest earthquake in history' is rising +38%, and this adds a historical, document-driven quake story the backlog hasn't told.

topics.title: The Aral Sea: A Sea That Vanished in a Lifetime
topics.core_question: How did one of the largest inland seas on Earth break into fragments within fifty years, and what did it leave behind?
topics.why_they_click: You can watch an entire sea disappear in satellite imagery, decade by decade, while the port towns sit stranded in desert.
topics.data_source: NASA Earth Observatory satellite imagery; USGS and international basin assessment reports; peer-reviewed Aral Sea desiccation studies
topics.evidence: 'geology documentary' is rising +5500%, the biggest trend in the dataset, and this topic is the most visually self-evident one on the list.

topics.title: Mount Pelée 1902: The Survivors of Saint-Pierre
topics.core_question: Why did the 1902 eruption of Mount Pelée destroy Saint-Pierre almost completely, and how did a handful of people live through it?
topics.why_they_click: A volcano gave weeks of warning before it killed a city in minutes — and the survivors' accounts are on the record.
topics.data_source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program; USGS Volcano Hazards Program; peer-reviewed Mount Pelée 1902 studies
topics.evidence: Volcano disasters are the channel's proven ground (St. Helens, Tambora, Krakatoa in the backlog), and this one comes with named eyewitness testimony.
